title: Regular casual work and a formal unfair-dismissal finding can still leave income restoration unresolved
source_unit: Fair Work Commission decision [2025] FWC 561 concerning a regular casual nail technician's dismissal
geography: Perth, Western Australia; Fair Work Commission U2024/9845

observations.period: February 2023 through February 24, 2025; regular casual work, dismissal, merits hearing, and deferred remedy

regular_work.value: The worker worked every week as a regular casual nail technician, usually 16 to 23 hours, and supplied 85 payslips in the jurisdictional dispute

dismissal.value: The employer dismissed the worker on August 1, 2024 after disputed complaints about client service, language, booking changes, and service timing

procedural_finding.value: The Commission held that the worker was protected by the unfair-dismissal jurisdiction and that the dismissal was harsh, unjust, and unreasonable; the decision records no formal warning or adequate opportunity to respond

remedy_and_livelihood.value: Remedy was deferred for further evidence and conciliation; payment, reinstatement, alternative employment, earnings recovery, and later livelihood are not established

mechanism.value: Legal recognition of regular-casual status and procedural unfairness can protect voice at adjudication while leaving the practical cost of lost work and remedy access with the worker

observations.method: Structured extraction from the primary Fair Work Commission decision [2025] FWC 561; regular work, neurodivergence disclosure, dismissal, jurisdiction, merits finding, and deferred remedy are kept separate.
observations.uncertainty: The public decision does not retain private payroll and household records, exact lost earnings, remedy amount, payment or reinstatement, alternative work, health effects, or later trust and livelihood outcomes.
observations.subgroup: One publicly adjudicated regular-casual worker in a small-firm employment case; no population denominator or comparison group is supplied.
observations.counterinterpretation: A regular work pattern and an unfair-dismissal finding do not establish that dismissal lacked any substantive concern, that reinstatement was feasible, or that a later remedy restored income or dignity.

boundary: This record establishes regular-casual work, a dismissal, formal recognition of jurisdiction and procedural unfairness, and a deferred remedy process. It does not establish final remedy receipt, recovered earnings, alternative work, household recovery, health outcome, trust change, recurrence, or exit.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The hash covers the compact project event ledger derived from the primary FWC decision; private payroll, medical, client, household, and later employment files are not retained.
